purpose: Pre-registration for Milestone 4. Committed before any claim is scored; harness.py refuses to score claims if this file has uncommitted changes, and records its SHA-256 and the git commit in results.json.
corpus: Wells/ICIT transcription via sequence_analysis/corpus.load_wells(): single-line, every sign readable, one copy per text, reading order. A text is scored only if every sign in it has a value in the key under test; that set of texts is fixed for all shuffled keys.

yajnadevam-2024-11-30.source: github.com/yajnadevam/lipi src/assets/data/xlits.csv @ eeeea5915ea3ed59fd37fc3a0f4e35ecc55aa6c5 (closest to the paper of 13 Nov 2024)
yajnadevam-2024-11-30.flag: per-sign substitution; the claimant's conjunct and vowel choices are not applied (the collapsed consonant skeleton makes them irrelevant)

yajnadevam-2026-07-15.flag: per-sign substitution; the claimant's conjunct and vowel choices are not applied (the collapsed consonant skeleton makes them irrelevant)

shaw-2026.test: do values follow the sign numbering: share of consecutive-number sign pairs whose values share a vowel, against values shuffled across signs

fuls-2024.source: paragorth/Indus- @ b2df930e87d2c5c7eaf1e1744d56d00dd2b7bff9, transcription of Fuls 2024 (IJAS 14(1)); values from Desset et al. 2022
fuls-2024.reason: no openly licensed Linear Elamite target corpus; coverage of the Wells corpus is reported only

bonta-2023.reason: key recoverable only from per-text readings that are not openly available

anonymous-614-page-dictionary.reason: key recoverable only from per-text readings

representation: collapsed consonant skeleton (decipherment/data.py skeleton): vowels, punctuation, anusvara and visarga removed; consonants reduced to the 16 the key distinguishes (k g c j t d n p b m y r l v s h). Applied identically to the key output, the target corpus, the control corpus and the positive-control plaintext.
target: Sanskrit: Digital Corpus of Sanskrit (CC BY 4.0) @ 8aeed5a1343d0e48b64eb32af8c00e8c6eb29359, texts Arthasastra, Manusmrti, Amarakosa, Hitopadesa, Kumarasambhava; about 10% of chapters held out for the positive control
control: Old Tamil: Project Madurai Sangam anthologies pmuni0028, 0057, 0110, 0229, 0296 (redistribution allowed with header); SHA-256 recorded at first fetch

scorers.sequence: primary (v2). (log2 P_trigram - log2 P_letters) per phoneme, end of text counted; both from the same Sanskrit corpus, interpolated Witten-Bell (sequence_analysis/ngram.py) over the skeleton alphabet
scorers.margin_tamil: v1 primary, kept and reported. (log2 P_Sanskrit trigram - log2 P_Old Tamil trigram) per phoneme
scorers.naive_bayes: rubric scorer. Multinomial Naive Bayes over character 1-3-grams (scikit-learn, lowercase=False), fitted only on Sanskrit vs Old Tamil lines; score = sum of per-n-gram log-likelihood ratios per phoneme

nulls.value_shuffle: the claim's own values permuted across shuffle units; a unit is a group of signs sharing (canonical head, value) and gets one value
nulls.binned_10: values permuted only within 10 equal-count bins of corpus token frequency

multiple_comparisons: Holm across 2 key versions x 3 scorers x 2 nulls = 12 tests; sensitivity runs reported outside the family
search_matched_null: run only if a key beats binned_10 after Holm: 20 hill-climbs x 2,000 value swaps against the same scorer, the claim compared with the distribution of optimised scores
positive_control: held-out DCS skeleton text segmented greedily (longest match) into the key's value skeletons, enciphered many-to-one with the key's own sign-value relation, cut to the Wells length distribution; 20 replicates x corruption 0, 10, 20, 30% of units, 1,000 draws per null; power = share with p < 0.05 under the primary score
negative_control: 200 value-shuffled tables treated as claims, each against 199 value-shuffle draws; p-values should be uniform (KS test), primary score
fitting_check: Yajnadevam's read texts vs unread texts in inscriptions.csv (no ref rows, unread texts that duplicate a read text removed), per-text margin, permutation of labels within sign-count strata (2,000 permutations)
not_used: dictionary hit rate (the least robust score: a large dictionary matches almost any syllable string); the vowel-freedom null (made redundant by the consonant skeleton, which ignores every vowel choice)
wording: Under {scorer} and {null} the table scores at percentile {P} (p = {p}); beating the frequency-matched null is necessary, not sufficient.
Not distinguishable from frequency-matched random tables under {scorer}; the harness detects true keys in {power}% of positive-control runs at this length.
revision: Version 1 (commit 9d89ed1) made 'Sanskrit minus Old Tamil' the primary score. Its first end-to-end run (a quick run, 300 shuffles, which also scored the two claims) showed that the positive control had 0% power against the value-shuffle null: Tamil script does not mark voicing, so the Old Tamil model makes any output rich in g, j, d, b look Sanskrit, whatever the sign order, and shuffled keys can score higher than the true key on real enciphered Sanskrit. Version 2 makes the primary score the Sanskrit trigram minus Sanskrit letter frequencies (order beyond letters), chosen because it had 100% power in a 10-replicate positive-control comparison of three candidate scores; the claims' scores were not used to choose it. The v1 score and the Naive Bayes score are still computed and reported, and all three are in the Holm family. Because v2 was fixed after the v1 quick run had scored the claims, this is disclosed in the report.
